category.text: $course$/top/Java Zero-to-Hired/Phase 2/5.6 System design basics for junior interviews

questiontext.text:
An interviewer says: 'Design a transfer API for a digital bank.' and waits.

What is the best first move?

generalfeedback.text: Requirements and assumptions frame every later choice; interviewers assess this structure.

answer.text: Draw Kafka, Kubernetes and ten microservices
Start writing Java code
Ask which cloud provider the bank uses and stop there
Clarify functional and non-functional requirements (scale, consistency, availability, compliance) and state assumptions

questiontext.text:
A bank expects 4 million transfers per day.

Roughly what average request rate is that, and what should you plan for?

answer.text: About 46,000 per second
About 4 per second; peaks don't matter
About 4,000 per second on average
About 46 per second on average; plan for peaks several times higher

questiontext.text:
A team proposes caching account balances in Redis for 60 seconds to speed up transfer authorisation.

What is the main problem?

generalfeedback.text: Cache read-mostly data that tolerates staleness, not data used to authorise money movement.

answer.text: Redis can't store decimals
60 seconds is too short for any cache
Stale balances could authorise debits that overdraw accounts; balances used for decisions must come from the source of truth under a lock
Caches always slow systems down

questiontext.text:
Statement queries overload the primary database. The team adds an asynchronous read replica for statements.

What trade-off must they handle?

generalfeedback.text: Async replicas can be behind; design for read-your-own-writes where it matters.

answer.text: Replication lag: a customer may not immediately see a transfer they just made, so recent activity may need to come from the primary
Replicas can't run SELECT queries
Replicas remove the need for backups
Replicas double write throughput

questiontext.text:
After a transfer, the API calls SMS, email and fraud services synchronously, and an SMS outage makes transfers time out.

What design change helps most?

generalfeedback.text: Queues decouple slow or failing follow-up work from the critical path.

answer.text: Retry the whole transfer when SMS fails
Add a longer timeout to the SMS call
Remove fraud scoring
Commit the transfer, publish an event (via an outbox) to a queue, and let consumers process notifications independently with retries

questiontext.text:
Which statements about horizontal scaling of a Spring Boot API are true? (Choose two.)

Select two.

generalfeedback.text: Stateless instances behind a load balancer scale out; shared state and locks must move to shared infrastructure.

answer.text: In-memory locks and rate limits stop working correctly across instances
It automatically scales the database
It removes the need for health checks
Instances should be stateless so any instance can serve any request

questiontext.text:
An interviewer asks how your payment hub behaves when a provider times out after possibly charging the customer.

What is the strongest answer?

generalfeedback.text: Unknown outcomes need resolution, not guesses; idempotency and status checks prevent double charges.

answer.text: Retry the charge until it succeeds
Record the payment as pending, resolve the outcome with status queries or webhooks, and never retry the charge blindly
Ask the customer to try again
Treat every timeout as a failure and refund

category.text: $course$/top/Java Zero-to-Hired/Phase 2/8.6 Working in an agile team

questiontext.text:
You pick up a ticket titled 'Improve reversals' with no description, and the sprint started today.

What should you do first?

generalfeedback.text: A ticket isn't ready without shared understanding and acceptance criteria.

answer.text: Start coding what you think it means
Move it to Done to keep velocity up
Ask the product owner and team to clarify the goal and agree acceptance criteria before starting
Split it by layer into database and API tickets

questiontext.text:
You have been stuck for most of a day on a failing Testcontainers setup, after trying the usual fixes.

What is the most professional action?

generalfeedback.text: Raising blockers early, with evidence of what you tried, protects the sprint.

answer.text: Keep quiet and work late until it's solved
Raise it as a blocker at stand-up or in the team chat, saying what you've tried, and ask for a pairing session
Re-estimate the ticket to 13 points silently
Delete the integration tests

questiontext.text:
A large story 'Customers can manage beneficiaries' is estimated at 21 points.

Which split is best?

generalfeedback.text: Vertical slices deliver testable behaviour in each piece.

answer.text: Vertical slices such as 'add a beneficiary with name enquiry', 'list beneficiaries', 'delete a beneficiary', each testable end to end
Database tables, then services, then controllers, then UI
One ticket per developer regardless of behaviour
Keep it as one story but work faster

questiontext.text:
Your feature works on your laptop, but the PR isn't reviewed and the integration tests haven't run in CI.

According to a typical definition of done, is the ticket done?

generalfeedback.text: Done means meeting the team's written definition of done, not just working locally.

answer.text: No: it needs review, merge, green CI and quality gates, updated docs, and deployment to the test environment
Yes, if the product owner liked the screenshot
Yes, if you add a TODO comment
Yes, it works locally

questiontext.text:
Which details make a bug report actionable? (Choose two.)

Select two.

generalfeedback.text: Reproducible steps and evidence get bugs fixed; personal data must never be included.

answer.text: A sentence saying 'it is broken again'
Exact steps to reproduce with environment and build version
The customer's full card number and BVN
Expected versus actual result with evidence such as a correlation id

questiontext.text:
During planning poker, you estimate 8 points and a senior engineer estimates 2.

What should happen next?

generalfeedback.text: Divergent estimates are a prompt to discuss assumptions.

answer.text: Remove the ticket from the sprint
Take the average, 5, and move on
Both explain their reasoning; the difference often reveals a misunderstanding or a missing task
Defer to the senior engineer without discussion

questiontext.text:
A bank requires a change approval (CAB) before production releases.

What helps your change get approved quickly?

generalfeedback.text: Auditors and approvers rely on linked, reviewed and tested evidence.

answer.text: Combining many unrelated changes into one release
Traceability: ticket with acceptance criteria, linked PR with review, green pipeline and test evidence, and a rollback plan
Releasing late at night to avoid questions
Skipping the ticket and merging directly

category.text: $course$/top/Java Zero-to-Hired/Phase 2/7.1 Unit testing with JUnit and Mockito; test-driven development

questiontext.text:
An integration test calls an @Async notification and then Thread.sleep(3000) before asserting. It is slow and still fails occasionally on the CI runner.

What is the better approach?

generalfeedback.text: Awaitility waits only as long as needed; synchronous executors remove the timing problem in unit tests.

answer.text: Run the test three times and accept any pass
Increase the sleep to 10 seconds
Use Awaitility to poll for the expected result with a timeout, or make the work synchronous in the test with a direct executor
Mark the test @Disabled on CI

category.text: $course$/top/Java Zero-to-Hired/Phase 2/7.2 Integration tests with Testcontainers (real Postgres, Kafka,

questiontext.text:
A suite of 40 test classes starts 25 Spring application contexts. Each class declares a slightly different set of @MockitoBean fields and properties.

Why is the suite slow, and what helps?

generalfeedback.text: Spring reuses a context only for identical configurations; @DirtiesContext makes it worse by discarding contexts.

answer.text: Each distinct configuration creates a new cached context; unify mocks and properties in a shared base or composed annotation
@MockitoBean must be replaced with @DirtiesContext
The JVM needs more heap
Testcontainers is always slow; remove it

category.text: $course$/top/Java Zero-to-Hired/Phase 2/7.4 Coverage with JaCoCo and static analysis with SonarQube

questiontext.text:
An ADR says controllers must never call repositories directly, but new code keeps doing it and reviewers miss it.

How can the build enforce the rule?

generalfeedback.text: ArchUnit turns architecture decisions into fast, automated tests.

answer.text: Raise the JaCoCo threshold
Add an ArchUnit test that fails when classes in the web package depend on the repository package
Run SonarQube once a month
Add a comment to every controller
